images.prompt: Create a refined naturalistic editorial dog portrait, native output exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2. One mature adult Dachshund, Standard, entirely visible in an original relaxed three-quarter standing pose at dog-eye level. Elongated low but sturdy muscular body; deep oval chest and prominent forechest; level back, slight tuck-up, four short articulated legs. Forefeet compact, broad and modestly larger than hindfeet; no extreme crookedness or knuckling. Tapered long head with slightly arched skull and very shallow stop; long strong muzzle, snug lips, dark almond eyes, black nose; moderate-length rounded pendant ears framing cheeks. Natural intact tail continues the spine without kink or tight curl. Real mature adult proportions, no giant head or stunted toy body. Standard-size adult with robust well-muscled trunk and substantial forechest. Choose one valid smooth-coated black-and-tan representative: close short shining coat, restrained tan eyebrow dots, tan muzzle sides/chest/legs and underside of tail, black nose and dark eyes. All four separate coherent paws must contact clear flat ground, with visible toes, no grass concealing them; clearly show anatomically attached full tail from its base to tip. Dog fills the scene gracefully while ample natural margin surrounds all ears, nose, paws and tail. Restrained lifelike fine fur texture, quiet field-guide elegance, believable soft daylight, crisp dog and softly receding backdrop. Original composition not based on any specific photograph. profileEvidence.author: B
profileEvidence.summary: Standard Dachshunds are typically bold, lively and persistent, with a willingness to follow scent and keep working when the job becomes difficult. Developed for hunting above and below ground, they can track, flush and retrieve as well as enter burrows. Standard denotes the larger size, which includes smooth, long-haired and wire-haired dogs rather than a single coat type.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: A bold, persistent scent hunter, the standard Dachshund belongs to the larger size across all three coat varieties.
